headline: PM Tarique Rahman visits Malaysia and China on first state visit
summary: The Prime Minister will focus on opening the labor market, ASEAN membership, and signing 17 agreements, including 13 MoUs, during his first official foreign tour.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is heading to Malaysia and China for his first state visit since forming the government. He is scheduled to depart from Dhaka at 3 PM on Sunday, June 21.

In Kuala Lumpur, the Prime Minister will hold an official meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Monday. Key discussion points will include opening the labor market, obtaining ASEAN membership, and free trade agreements.
The visit to Malaysia is also expected to result in the signing of several agreements, including those focused on cultural exchange.
On Tuesday, the Prime Minister will travel directly to Dalian, China, to attend the 17th Annual Meeting of the World Economic Forum's 'New Champions' (2026 Summer Davos Forum).
While in China, he is expected to meet with several world leaders and will hold a bilateral meeting with the Chinese Prime Minister on Wednesday.
The visit to China is expected to result in the signing of a total of 17 agreements, including 13 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs).
The Prime Minister will also meet with President Xi Jinping on June 26, before returning to Bangladesh on the same night.
caption:
17 agreements and two major Asian powers. PM Tarique Rahman begins his first state visit today.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is heading to Malaysia and China for his first state visit since forming the government. He is scheduled to depart from Dhaka at 3 PM on Sunday, June 21.

In Kuala Lumpur, the Prime Minister will hold an official meeting with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Monday. Key discussion points will include opening the labor market, obtaining ASEAN membership, and free trade agreements.

The visit to Malaysia is also expected to result in the signing of several agreements, including those focused on cultural exchange.

On Tuesday, the Prime Minister will travel directly to Dalian, China, to attend the 17th Annual Meeting of the World Economic Forum's 'New Champions' (2026 Summer Davos Forum).

While in China, he is expected to meet with several world leaders and will hold a bilateral meeting with the Chinese Prime Minister on Wednesday.

The visit to China is expected to result in the signing of a total of 17 agreements, including 13 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs).

The Prime Minister will also meet with President Xi Jinping on June 26, before returning to Bangladesh on the same night.
